Hands-on Exercise 10

Information Dashboard Design

Author

ZeXin Chen

Published

June 22, 2026

Modified

June 22, 2026

1 Overview

In this hands-on exercise we learn to design the building blocks of an information dashboard in R. We cover three things:

  • bullet charts and sparklines drawn with ggplot2
  • static dashboard tables built with gt and gtExtras
  • interactive dashboard tables built with reactable and reactablefmtr

A dashboard packs a lot of numbers into a small space, so the design principle throughout is restraint. We use plain backgrounds, a single highlight colour for the value that matters, and grey for everything that is context.

2 Getting Started

2.1 Installing and Loading Packages

pacman::p_load(lubridate, ggthemes, reactable,
               reactablefmtr, gt, gtExtras, tidyverse)

The interactive sparklines in the last section need the dataui package, which lives on GitHub rather than CRAN. Install it once with the line below, then it loads with the others.

remotes::install_github("timelyportfolio/dataui")
library(dataui)

3 The Data

The data is a personal sales database for a coffee chain. The original file is in Microsoft Access format, which needs the RODBC package and a 32 bit R session to read. To avoid that, we use the prepared CoffeeChain.rds file, which holds the same query table already converted to an R data frame.

coffeechain <- read_rds("data/rds/CoffeeChain.rds")

4 Bullet Chart in ggplot2

A bullet chart compares an actual value against a target, using shaded bands for context. It is a compact alternative to a gauge. First we aggregate sales and budgeted sales by product.

product <- coffeechain %>%
  group_by(`Product`) %>%
  summarise(`target` = sum(`Budget Sales`),
            `current` = sum(`Sales`)) %>%
  ungroup()

The chart layers grey context bands behind a black measure bar, with a red marker for the target. Colour is used sparingly here: grey for the qualitative ranges, black for the actual value, and a single red line for the target.

  • The Plot
  • The Code
ggplot(product, aes(Product, current)) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, max(target) * 1.01),
           fill = "grey85", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, target * 0.75),
           fill = "grey60", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, target * 0.5),
           fill = "grey50", width = 0.85) +
  geom_col(aes(Product, current),
           width = 0.35,
           fill = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = target,
                    x = Product,
                    ymin = target,
                    ymax = target),
                width = .4,
                colour = "red",
                size = 1) +
  coord_flip()

5 Sparklines in ggplot2

A sparkline is a small line chart with no axes, meant to show the shape of a trend at a glance. We build one per product, faceted into a stack.

5.1 Preparing the Data

sales_report <- coffeechain %>%
  filter(Date >= "2013-01-01") %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date)) %>%
  group_by(Month, Product) %>%
  summarise(Sales = sum(Sales)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(Month, Product, Sales)

We mark the lowest month, the highest month, and the final month so each sparkline can be annotated.

mins <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>%
  slice(which.min(Sales))
maxs <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>%
  slice(which.max(Sales))
ends <- group_by(sales_report, Product) %>%
  filter(Month == max(Month))

We also compute the 25th and 75th percentiles so we can shade the interquartile band behind each line.

quarts <- sales_report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarise(quart1 = quantile(Sales, 0.25),
            quart2 = quantile(Sales, 0.75)) %>%
  right_join(sales_report)

5.2 Drawing the Sparklines

The grey band shows the normal range, the line shows the trend, the red point marks the lowest month and the blue point the highest. The Tufte theme strips away everything that is not data.

  • The Plot
  • The Code
ggplot(sales_report, aes(x = Month, y = Sales)) +
  facet_grid(Product ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
  geom_ribbon(data = quarts, aes(ymin = quart1, max = quart2),
              fill = 'grey90') +
  geom_line(size = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = mins, col = 'red') +
  geom_point(data = maxs, col = 'blue') +
  geom_text(data = mins, aes(label = Sales), vjust = -1) +
  geom_text(data = maxs, aes(label = Sales), vjust = 2.5) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = Sales), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = ends, aes(label = Product), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1.0) +
  expand_limits(x = max(sales_report$Month) +
                  (0.25 * (max(sales_report$Month) - min(sales_report$Month)))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 12, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.1, 0)) +
  theme_tufte(base_size = 3, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_blank())

6 Static Dashboard with gt and gtExtras

The gt package builds presentation tables, and gtExtras adds dashboard elements such as inline bullet charts and sparklines. These tables are the static building blocks of a report dashboard.

6.1 Simple Bullet Chart Table

gt_plt_bullet() draws an inline bullet chart in each row, comparing the current value against its target. The light blue bar is the actual value, the black line the target.

product %>%
  gt::gt() %>%
  gt_plt_bullet(column = current,
                target = target,
                width = 60,
                palette = c("lightblue", "black")) %>%
  gt_theme_538()
Product current

Caffe Latte
Caffe Mocha
Chamomile
Colombian

6.2 Preparing the Monthly Report

For sparklines in a table, gtExtras needs the monthly sales for each product collected into a list column.

report <- coffeechain %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date)) %>%
  filter(Year == "2013") %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date,
                       label = TRUE,
                       abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(Product, Month) %>%
  summarise(Sales = sum(Sales)) %>%
  ungroup()

6.3 Sparkline Table

gt_plt_sparkline() turns each product’s list of monthly sales into an inline sparkline.

report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize('Monthly Sales' = list(Sales),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline('Monthly Sales',
                   same_limit = FALSE)
Product Monthly Sales

6.4 Adding Summary Statistics

We can place summary numbers next to the sparkline. First the spark list column, then the min, max and average, then join them.

spark <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize('Monthly Sales' = list(Sales),
            .groups = "drop")
sales <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarise("Min" = min(Sales, na.rm = T),
            "Max" = max(Sales, na.rm = T),
            "Average" = mean(Sales, na.rm = T))
sales_data <- left_join(sales, spark)
sales_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline('Monthly Sales',
                   same_limit = FALSE)

6.5 Combining Bullet Chart and Sparklines

A full dashboard row can carry both the trend and the target comparison. We add the target and actual totals, then draw a sparkline and a bullet chart side by side.

bullet <- coffeechain %>%
  filter(Date >= "2013-01-01") %>%
  group_by(`Product`) %>%
  summarise(`Target` = sum(`Budget Sales`),
            `Actual` = sum(`Sales`)) %>%
  ungroup()
sales_data <- sales_data %>%
  left_join(bullet)
sales_data %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_plt_sparkline('Monthly Sales') %>%
  gt_plt_bullet(column = Actual,
                target = Target,
                width = 28,
                palette = c("lightblue", "black")) %>%
  gt_theme_538()

7 Interactive Dashboard with reactable and reactablefmtr

The reactable package builds interactive tables, and reactablefmtr adds interactive sparklines that respond to hovering. These are the building blocks of a live dashboard.

7.1 Preparing the List Column

Like gtExtras, reactablefmtr needs the monthly sales as a list column.

report <- report %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarize(`Monthly Sales` = list(Sales))

7.2 Basic Interactive Sparklines

react_sparkline() draws an interactive sparkline in each row. Hovering over a line reveals the underlying values.

reactable(
  report,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(report)
    )
  )
)

7.3 Showing All Rows

By default the table pages at 10 rows. Setting defaultPageSize to 13 shows every product on one page.

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(report)
    )
  )
)

7.4 Adding Points and Labels

highlight_points marks the lowest and highest months in red and blue, and labels prints the first and last values.

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(
        report,
        highlight_points = highlight_points(
          min = "red", max = "blue"),
        labels = c("first", "last")
      )
    )
  )
)

7.5 Adding a Reference Line

statline draws a reference line, here the mean of each product’s monthly sales.

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(
        report,
        highlight_points = highlight_points(
          min = "red", max = "blue"),
        statline = "mean"
      )
    )
  )
)

7.6 Adding a Bandline

Instead of a reference line, a band can show the interquartile range behind the sparkline.

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkline(
        report,
        highlight_points = highlight_points(
          min = "red", max = "blue"),
        line_width = 1,
        bandline = "innerquartiles",
        bandline_color = "green"
      )
    )
  )
)

7.7 Sparkbars Instead of Sparklines

The same data can be shown as small bars rather than a line, using react_sparkbar().

reactable(
  report,
  defaultPageSize = 13,
  columns = list(
    Product = colDef(maxWidth = 200),
    `Monthly Sales` = colDef(
      cell = react_sparkbar(
        report,
        highlight_bars = highlight_bars(
          min = "red", max = "blue"),
        bandline = "innerquartiles",
        statline = "mean")
    )
  )
)
